economy.summary: His official House biography says that during his tenure he has championed legislation to reduce government control, lower taxes, and promote a strong economy.
economy.short: Champions legislation to reduce government control, promote strong economy.

taxes.summary: In November 2025 he voted for the $50.1 billion 2025-26 state budget, saying it contained significant long-term wins for Somerset County residents, including a requirement that state regulators speed up the permitting process.
taxes.short: Voted for $50.1 billion 2025-26 budget, citing permitting reform.

abortion.summary: In July 2022 he voted for Senate Bill 106, a proposed constitutional amendment providing that the Pennsylvania Constitution contains no right to taxpayer-funded abortion or any other right relating to abortion.
abortion.short: Voted for amendment stating no constitutional right to abortion.

education.summary: In July 2024 he voted against the state budget bill but supported the accompanying education code bill directing how school funding is used, which included charter school funding reform and grant funding for school security, including armed security, provisions drawn from a bill he had previously introduced.
education.short: Supported education code with charter funding reform, school security grants.

energy.summary: Explaining his 2025-26 budget vote, he called Pennsylvania's removal from the Regional Greenhouse Gas Initiative the biggest victory, describing RGGI as a carbon tax program he says cost the state energy jobs and economic development, and said the state can now export more energy to lower costs and support jobs.
energy.short: Supports RGGI exit; says state can export more energy.

guns.summary: His official House biography describes him as a strong protector of the Second Amendment who upholds the principle that the right of the people to keep and bear arms shall not be questioned.
guns.short: Strong Second Amendment protector; right shall not be questioned.
